column15: I'm really concerned about the insertion of advertisements in AI software. In our daily lives， we use AI software almost every day. If the advertisements are very obvious， we can identify them. However， for some hidden advertisements， due to our trust in AI， we often fail to notice their existence， leading to unconscious biased choices. This is very scary.
column17:
AI has a strong guiding influence. When making decisions we are uncertain about， we often turn to AI as a guide for our actions. If AI inserts hard-to-detect advertisements into its responses， on one hand， people may struggle to notice these ads， leading them to make decisions they otherwise wouldn’t have. On the other hand， embedding ads in AI’s response systems could trigger a crisis of trust. When using AI， people may constantly worry whether the answers are truly objective or algorithmically delivered advertisements.
Mainstream applications like ChatGPT and DeepSeek are chatbot programs. Unlike traditional web ads or video pre-roll ads， inserting advertisements into such interactive software would allow ads to reach potential customers with unprecedented precision. For advertisers， this would indeed be an excellent method， avoiding the cost inefficiencies of mass advertising. However， for consumers， such manipulation could be highly dangerous—much like in The Truman Show， where no one knows whether they are living in the real world or a carefully constructed reality shaped by advertisers.

column17:
Including advertisement recommendations in large language models is a double-edged sword. On one hand， it can create value for companies; on the other hand， if the ads are too frequent or lack transparency， they may undermine user experience and trust. The key lies in ensuring the relevance and quality of the recommendations， as well as giving users a certain degree of control — ads should not overly interfere with the user experience. 
Moreover， commercial competition is another important factor: the presence or absence of appropriate ad recommendations might become a new dimension in the competition between AI models. Users may prefer AI systems that are efficient and relatively ad-free. 
Additionally， overly intelligent ad recommendations might raise concerns among users， making them wary of AI that feels too smart — going beyond the role of a tool.
